rationale: Both legs are essentially profitability scaled by a balance-sheet stock (oiadp/at and oibdp/lt are highly correlated), so the "bottleneck" MIN is a cosmetic operator swap on the archive's already-tested SelfFinancedProfitPower/TroughProfitSolvency rank-composite of profitability and profit-to-liability coverage rather than a genuine new interaction.

EBITDA-less-interest over total liabilities is a textbook debt-service-coverage/credit-quality metric (an Ohlson/Piotroski-style ingredient), and since xint is small relative to oibdp the measure is dominated by oibdp/lt, making it a single-ratio profitability-scaled-by-liabilities sort very close to the archive's oancf/lt leg rather than a cross-theme interaction.

The working-capital-intensity leg is close to the known net-operating-assets/accruals anomaly, but the sign orientation is correct and consistent with that literature, and conditioning profitability on operating-cycle cash intensity is a coherent, non-trivial interaction — the main risks are sale-in-denominator instability for low-revenue firms and coverage loss from act/lct.

The Δleverage leg is close to the documented debt-issuance/net-external-financing anomaly, so part of the return is likely already spanned, but the expected sign is internally consistent and interacting financing direction with profitability is a legitimate and reasonably distinct test of "self-funded" operating strength.

Financing-policy stability is a plausibly less-mined channel than earnings stability and the expression matches the hypothesis, but a standard deviation estimated from three annual leverage observations is extremely noisy and will largely proxy for asset growth/issuance activity, so the effective information content may be thin.

The effective-interest term xint/lt has an order-of-magnitude smaller cross-sectional dispersion than oiadp/at (and is downward-biased and noisy because lt includes non-interest-bearing liabilities), so the spread will correlate near-unity with a plain ROA sort — a rediscovery of the profitability anomaly dressed as a cost-of-capital spread.
